sections.content: You know the reporting verbs *afirmar*, *señalar* and *negar* from B2 Unit 18, and the time words of retelling (*al día siguiente*, *el día anterior*) from B2 Unit 17. A news report is built on them: the writer names who said it, then reports it. Use *afirmar que* or *señalar que* + the indicative for what someone states: *El portavoz afirmó que el incendio estaba controlado.* Use *negar que* + the subjunctive for a claim someone rejects: *Las autoridades negaron que hubiera heridos.* After a past verb the tenses move back, and *mañana* becomes *al día siguiente*: *El portavoz anunció que darían a conocer el balance al día siguiente.*

sections.title: What the verb tells you
rows: El portavoz afirmó que el fuego estaba controlado.
The spokesperson stated that the fire was under control. (indicative)
Las autoridades negaron que hubiera heridos.
The authorities denied that there were any injured. (subjunctive)
Los bomberos señalaron que habían evacuado el edificio.
The firefighters pointed out that they had evacuated the building. (indicative)
Anunció que darían un balance al día siguiente.
He announced that they would give a summary the next day. (mañana becomes al día siguiente)

sections.content: Do not use one verb for everything. *Decir* is neutral, but *afirmar*, *señalar* and *negar* tell the reader how the statement was made, and *negar* changes the mood. Then check the shifts: after a past reporting verb use *estaba*, *hubiera*, *darían*, and say *al día siguiente*, not *mañana*. Do not add *de* before *que*: *negaron que*, not *negaron de que*.
